images.name: ice_peak_01
images.prompt: Generate ONE ice impact peak primitive. Output requested: exactly 512x512 transparent RGBA PNG, body about 260x220 actual pixels. The previous attempt was oversized: do not fill the canvas. If your native canvas must be 1254x1254, keep the body only 260x220 actual pixels centered (roughly 21 percent of canvas width and 18 percent of canvas height); very broad fully transparent margins are intentional. One connected dense off-centre crystalline impact core, SIX straight-edged angular wedges of clearly unequal lengths radiating outward and upward; two or three have broken angular notches mid-length but remain attached. Asymmetric and wider than tall, upright facing the elevated approximately 45-degree game camera. Match the attached approved fire impact's visual LANGUAGE only: confident hand-drawn near-black tapered contour, exactly four flat hard-edged grayscale planes. Ice vocabulary is crystalline facets and sharp points. Palette exclusively #202020 contour and thin rim, #606060 shadowed facets, #bfbfbf majority lit facets, #ffffff brightest edges and densest core at most one fifth of painted area. Each facet boundary has a dark tapered hand-drawn line. Completely uniform solid flat fills, ZERO gradients or texture within each plane. One frame of hand-drawn painted 2D effects animation, clean planes and small silhouette readability. Key edge facing screen upper-left. Attached Image 1 is scale/register board, Image 2 fire peak is style language only, Image 3 native scene reading only. No curls, rounded tongues, symmetry, star, snowflake, extra detached fragments, glow, blur, mist, sparkles, ground, shadows, characters, text, panels or checkerboard. Paint only emission shape; lighting and motion will be added at runtime. Real transparency: alpha zero outside, fully opaque interior, crisp perimeter with at most one pixel antialiasing. If actual transparency impossible, only flat pure #00ff00 background. Request again native 512x512 PNG with 260x220 painted extent; never enlarge the painted body to fill a larger native canvas.
